message.content:
Sure thing! 🎉 Below’s a quick “starter kit” you can tweak as much (or little) as you’d like:

| What | Why it matters | Quick tip |
|------|-----------------|-----------|
| **Dates & Duration** | Helps lock flight prices & hotel availability | Aim for mid‑week stays; weekdays often cheaper than weekends. |
| **Budget** | Guides choice between luxury vs. boutique hotels, fine dining vs. street food | Rough rule: €150–€250/night per person for decent lodging + meals. |
| **Interests** | Tailors your day‑to‑day agenda – art lovers, history buffs, foodie explorers, shopaholics, romance seekers… | List top 5 things you *must* see/try. |
| **Travel Style** | Influences transportation choices (public transit pass vs. bike rental vs. walking). | A Navigo Week Pass (€22.80) covers metro, RER, buses, trams within zones 1‑2. |

---

### Sample Itinerary (7 days)

> **Day 0:** Arrive → Check into hotel / Airbnb near central arrondissements (e.g., Marais, Latin Quarter, Saint‑Germain).
>
> **Day 1:** Classic landmarks  
> - Morning: Louvre (skip-the-line ticket recommended)  
> - Lunch at Café Marly (great view of Pyramid)  
> - Afternoon: Palais Royal gardens & boutiques  
> - Evening: Seine river cruise (Bateaux Mouches)
>
> **Day 2:** Art & Culture  
> - Musée d’Orsay (Impressionist masterpieces)  
> - Walk along Rue de Rivoli to Place Vendôme  
> - Dinner at Le Cinq (Michelin-starred) or cozy bistro in Montmartre
>
> **Day 3:** Day Trip Options  
> - Versailles Palace & Gardens (train TGV from Gare du Nord)  
>   OR  
> - Giverny (Monet’s garden) via train + bus combo
>
> **Day 4:** Neighborhood Exploration  
> - Canal Saint-Martin brunch spot (Le Comptoir Général)  
> - Explore trendy shops & vintage stalls  
> - Sunset picnic at Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
>
> **Day 5:** Foodie Focus  
> - Breakfast at L’As du Fallafel (Marais)  
> - Cooking class (French pastries or cheese tasting)  
> - Night market stroll (Marché Bastille if open)
>
> **Day 6:** Relaxation & Shopping  
> - Spa morning at Les Bains du Marais  
> - Champs‑Élysées window shopping → Arc de Triomphe climb  
> - Final dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking Eiffel Tower
>
> **Day 7:** Departure Prep  
> - Pack souvenirs from Galeries Lafayette or Printemps  
> - Last-minute coffee at Angelina (famous hot chocolate)  

Feel free to swap out activities—Paris has endless possibilities!

---

#### Practical Tips

| Topic | Recommendation |
|-------|---------------|
| **Flights** | Book early (~8 weeks ahead); consider airlines offering flexible change policies due to unpredictable schedules. |
| **Accommodation** | Look for properties with kitchenettes if staying >3 nights—you’ll save on breakfasts/dinners. |
| **Transport** | Get a multi-day Metro/RER pass; use Vélib' bikes for short hops (<10 km). |
| **Dining** | Reserve Michelin restaurants months before; try local markets (marchés) for fresh produce & charcuterie. |
| **Language** | Basic French phrases help; most Parisians speak English in tourist areas. |
| **Safety** | Keep valuables secure; avoid carrying all cash—use contactless payments where possible. |
| **Weather** | Spring (April–June): mild, occasional showers. Summer (July–August): warm, crowds high. Winter (Dec–Feb): chilly, fewer tourists. |

---

### Next Steps?

If you'd like a customized version:
1. Tell me how many days you’re planning to stay.  
2. Share your approximate daily budget.  
3. Let me know what kind of experiences excite you most (art, cuisine, nightlife, nature, etc.).  
4. Mention any special needs (dietary restrictions, mobility concerns).

Once I have those bits, I can craft a tailored schedule—including exact booking links, price ranges, and insider hacks—to make sure your Paris adventure hits all the right notes. 🚀
